scenario.description: An IP transactions counsel must approve a proposed trademark coexistence agreement with a competing brand and finalize its permitted territory, excluded sales channel, term, and quality-control protections, with input from trademark counsel and the brand partnerships lead.

shared_context.S1: The company is negotiating a coexistence agreement with Northstar Health, whose registered mark is similar to the company's new Vela mark.
shared_context.S2: The current draft does not specify the final permitted territory, excluded sales channel, agreement term, or quality-control rights.
shared_context.S3: Mara Chen has authority to approve the agreement before it is sent to Northstar Health.
shared_context.S4: The firm's standard matter-closing checklist requires trademark counsel and the business owner to state any unresolved legal or commercial issue before the approving counsel signs off.
shared_context.S5: The approval worksheet requires Mara to record final values for all four open terms during this meeting; any drafting work that remains afterward is recorded as a revision commitment rather than a reason to defer the decision. For this worksheet, the permitted territory must be recorded specifically as U.S. online marketplaces, not the broader United States.

PF1.text: While reviewing Northstar Health's earlier coexistence settlement with another mark owner, Elias confirmed that Northstar is bound to keep its similar mark out of U.S. brick-and-mortar retail but may use it in U.S. online marketplaces, and that the settlement requires an annual quality-control audit right for the other party; he has not yet added these restrictions to the current draft.

PF2.text: Nora confirmed in this week's launch-planning meeting that the company is reserving the enterprise-healthcare channel for Vela and has approved a five-year brand rollout plan; she has not yet put those commercial requirements into the agreement instructions.

acceptance_conditions: The agreement must be approved, or approval may be deferred only if the settlement includes a commitment to revise the coexistence draft.
The permitted territory must be U.S. online marketplaces specifically.
The enterprise-healthcare sales channel must be excluded from Northstar Health's permitted use.
The agreement term must be exactly five years.
The agreement must include an annual quality-control audit right.
The approval decision must cite Elias's disclosed prior-settlement finding as justification.

content_checks.C1: decisions['approve_agreement'] == True or (decisions['approve_agreement'] == False and any(c['type'] == 'draft_revision' or c['type'] == 'trademark_counsel_update' or c['type'] == 'coexistence_draft_revision' for c in commitments))
content_checks.C2: 'U.S.' in decisions['permitted_territory'] and 'online marketplace' in decisions['permitted_territory']
content_checks.C3: 'enterprise-healthcare' in decisions['excluded_sales_channel'] or 'enterprise healthcare' in decisions['excluded_sales_channel'] or ('enterprise' in decisions['excluded_sales_channel'] and 'healthcare' in decisions['excluded_sales_channel'])

decisive_facts.why: The current draft leaves the permitted territory and quality-control protection open; PF1 changes them to U.S. online marketplaces and an annual audit right.
The commercial plan changes the agreement from an unspecified channel and term to exclusion of enterprise healthcare and an exact five-year term.
